old: "A weak king of high birth or a strong king of low birth": "The constituent elements, having regard to weakness, go along with the instigation (upajāpa) of a weak king of high birth only with difficulty, but easily with that of a strong king of low birth, having regard to strength," say the teachers.

old: The constituent elements of their own accord submit to a weak king of high birth; the constituent element of sovereignty follows the well-born one.
new: The constituent elements of their own accord submit to a weak king of high birth; sovereignty by its nature follows the well-born one.
why: reviewer (error): aiśvarya is not one of the prakṛtis, and a singular 'constituent element of sovereignty' has no referent in the system; here prakṛti is used in its ordinary sense 'nature' (svabhāva): 'sovereignty by its nature attaches to the well-born'. The glossary rendering applies to prakṛti = the seven constituents, not to this sense. The Hindi 'ऐश्वर्य की प्रकृति' is fine, since प्रकृति also means nature.
reviewer (error): Same: gloss as 'the nature of sovereignty'.

old: aiśvarya-prakṛti: either 'the constituents (subjects) of the realm' or 'the nature of sovereignty', i.e. sovereignty by its nature attaches to high birth; glossary rendering kept.
new: aiśvarya-prakṛti taken as 'the nature (svabhāva) of sovereignty', i.e. sovereignty by its nature attaches to high birth; the alternative 'the constituents (subjects) of the realm' is possible but aiśvarya is not one of the seven prakṛtis. Hindi प्रकृति covers both senses.
why: reviewer (minor): Note should record the alternative the other way round (nature chosen, constituents as alternative).

old: और बलवान् अकुलीन राजा के उपजाप को वे विफल कर देती हैं; अनुराग में ही सब गुणों की पूर्णता है।
new: और बलवान् अकुलीन राजा के उपजाप को वे विफल कर देती हैं; अनुराग में सब गुणों की पूर्णता है।

old: And they frustrate the instigation of a strong king of low birth; in affection lies the totality of all qualities.
new: And they frustrate the secret instigation of a strong king of low birth; in affection lies the totality of all qualities.

old: Because it destroys the effort (spent on it), destruction of the standing crop is worse than destruction of the handful (the reaped grain); because it leaves no livelihood, drought is worse than excessive rain.
new: Because it destroys the effort (spent on it), destruction of the crop is worse than destruction of the handful; because it leaves no livelihood, drought is worse than excessive rain.
why: reviewer (minor): 'standing' and '(the reaped grain)' put one contested interpretation of muṣṭi into the translation. The causal reading of prayāsa-vadhāt is right (parallel to nirājīvatvāt), but the 'loss of effort' argument fits muṣṭi = the handful of seed sown (little effort lost) at least as well as reaped grain. Keep the translation literal and leave the interpretation in notes.
